harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented cross-LAN firewall between node2 (lan-a) and node3 (lan-b), routed through node1 (VyOS), entirely via Ansible run from the designated control node (node4). node2 can reach node3 on TCP/5432 only; all other inter-LAN traffic (other ports, ICMP, reverse-direction connections) is dropped. Playbook (/root/cross_lan_firewall.yml on node4) configures static systemd-networkd addressing/routing on node2/node3 and VyOS interface addresses + an ipv4 forward-filter firewall (default-action drop, established/related accept, explicit accept for 10.10.1.10->10.10.2.10 tcp/5432) on node1, applied via a rendered script run through SSH+sudo (the vyos.vyos network_cli module hit a reproducible device-side "Set failed" bug on the first live 'set' in every fresh CLI session, root cause traced to the vyos user's non-interactive cli-shell-api session context; running as root via sudo bypassed it cleanly). Verified from a fully clean state, confirmed persistence in /config/config.boot and netowrkd unit files, and completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all four nodes with boot_id proof and post-restart functional re-verification.
actions_performed: Explored topology: node1=VyOS router (eth0=mgmt/default net, eth1/eth2=lan-a/lan-b, unaddressed), node2=lan-a host (enp1s0=mgmt, enp8s0=lan-a, unaddressed), node3=lan-b host (enp1s0=mgmt, enp8s0=lan-b, unaddressed), node4=Ansible control node (ansible-core 2.20.5 preinstalled, no vyos.vyos collection)
Installed vyos.vyos ansible collection on node4

Bootstrapped SSH: generated missing sshd host keys and started ssh on node2/node3; added the control node's SSH key as a VyOS-managed authorized key for the 'vyos' user on node1 (via `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys`) and to node2/node3 root authorized_keys
Determined lan-a/lan-b subnet-to-interface mapping (eth1<->node2, eth2<->node3) via temporary IP assignment and ping tests

Diagnosed and root-caused a reproducible VyOS bug: vyos_config over ansible.netcommon network_cli genuinely fails 'Set failed' on the first live 'set' issued by the unprivileged 'vyos' user in any fresh CLI session (confirmed via -vvvv/ANSIBLE_LOG_PATH raw protocol trace and by isolating user vs SSH vs pty as variables); running the equivalent script as root (via sudo, since vyos has NOPASSWD ALL sudo) works reliably every time

Wrote /root/inventory.ini and /root/cross_lan_firewall.yml on node4: play 1 renders per-host systemd-networkd static address+route units on node2/node3 (become root) and restarts systemd-networkd; play 2 (become root on node1) renders and executes a script.template-based VyOS CLI script (interface addresses + firewall) then saves and cleans up

Validated end-to-end from a fully reset state (deleted all applied config, flushed addresses) by re-running the playbook and confirming state, then functionally verified with nc/ping: node2->node3:5432 succeeds, node2->node3 other port fails, node3->node2 reverse fails, ICMP both directions fails

Executed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured boot_id + service/data health baselines on all 4 nodes, restarted node4, node2, node3, then node1 one at a time via `systemctl reboot`, polled each until command execution returned, proved boot_id changed on every node, and re-verified functional recovery after each restart (ansible tooling on node4, static IP/route/sshd on node2 & node3, VyOS interface addresses + firewall config + working 5432 allow / everything-else block after node1's reboot)

evidence.requirement: Topology and image/user discovery (VyOS on node1, Ubuntu on node2/3/4, ansible-core on node4)
evidence.summary: Confirmed node1=VyOS 2026.04.02 rolling, node2/3/4=Ubuntu 24.04, node4 has ansible-core 2.20.5 and expects /root/inventory.ini + EXECUTED_FILE playbook per run.sh contract

evidence.requirement: lan-a/lan-b <-> node1 interface mapping determined empirically
evidence.summary: eth1 (node1) pings 10.10.1.254 from node2's enp8s0; eth2 (node1) pings 10.10.2.254 from node3's enp8s0, confirming eth1<->lan-a<->node2 and eth2<->lan-b<->node3

evidence.requirement: SSH access bootstrapped from control node to all managed nodes
evidence.summary: Generated sshd host keys + started ssh on node2/node3, added control node pubkey to node2/node3 root and to VyOS vyos user via system login config; verified passwordless SSH to all three managed nodes from node4

evidence.requirement: Root-caused vyos_config network_cli failure and validated the sudo-as-root workaround
evidence.summary: Raw protocol trace proved 'Set failed' is a genuine VyOS CLI rejection (not a pager artifact) specific to the unprivileged vyos user's non-interactive config session; identical script run via `sudo bash` as root succeeded and applied interface address to the live kernel state

evidence.requirement: Ansible playbook created and run from the designated control node (node4), applying static addressing/routing on node2/node3 and VyOS interface+firewall config on node1
evidence.summary: Full playbook run from a fully reset baseline (all config deleted, addresses flushed) completed with ok/changed on all three hosts: node1 rendered+applied VyOS config, node2/node3 got systemd-networkd static config and were restarted

evidence.requirement: Persisted VyOS state verified (survives beyond running-config)
evidence.summary: /config/config.boot on node1 shows eth1/eth2 addresses and the full firewall ipv4 forward filter (default-action drop, rule 5 established/related accept, rule 10 tcp/5432 accept 10.10.1.10->10.10.2.10); node2/node3 routes confirmed to the peer LAN via node1

evidence.requirement: Functional proof: node2 can reach node3 on TCP/5432 only; all other inter-LAN traffic is blocked
evidence.summary: nc test: node2->node3:5432 succeeds and payload received on node3; node2->node3:2222 fails; ICMP node2->node3 fails; reverse-direction node3->node2:5432 fails (no allow rule for that direction)

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: healthy baseline (boot_id + health) captured for every node before any restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, uptime -s, interface/route state, sshd status and firewall presence on node1/node2/node3/node4 prior to any restart

evidence.requirement: node4 restarted one at a time; boot_id changed; recovery proven
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued, connection reset confirms disruption, boot_id changed e796da36->78462094, ansible-playbook --check afterward proves tooling and connectivity to all managed nodes fully functional

evidence.requirement: node2 restarted one at a time; boot_id changed; recovery proven
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued, boot_id changed cf34dc87->53c5ab4b, static IP/route/sshd recovered post-boot, and the allowed 5432 flow to node3 still succeeds

evidence.requirement: node3 restarted one at a time; boot_id changed; recovery proven
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued, boot_id changed 96c08b66->e90f82ae, static IP/route/sshd recovered post-boot; post-reboot re-check confirms 5432 allowed and ICMP still blocked through node1

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS router) restarted one at a time last (most critical data path); boot_id changed; full config and enforcement recovery proven
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued, node1 unreachable through timeout/reset states during boot, boot_id changed 01e92881->811484d1 after ~4 minutes; post-reboot config.boot re-verified (interfaces + firewall persisted and re-applied to live interfaces), and final functional test confirms 5432 allow / other-port+ICMP+reverse-direction block all still enforced
